pharm: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that selectively relaxes vascular smooth muscle, reducing peripheral vascular resistance and lowering blood pressure.
quick: Start 5 mg once daily; usual range 2.5 to 10 mg once daily (extended-release)
Take consistently; avoid grapefruit/grapefruit juice (raises levels markedly)
Use only if clearly needed; alternatives often preferred
Unknown if excreted in human milk; use with caution
Start 2.5 mg once daily; monitor closely - reduced clearance
Blood pressure, heart rate, peripheral edema
summary: Felodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker, supplied as an extended-release tablet, indicated for the treatment of hypertension. It has greater selectivity for vascular smooth muscle than cardiac muscle, lowering peripheral resistance and blood pressure with little direct effect on cardiac contractility. The most common adverse effects are dose-related peripheral edema and headache. It is metabolized by CYP3A4, so grapefruit juice and CYP3A4 inhibitors can substantially raise its levels; CYP3A4 inducers reduce them.
indications: Treatment of hypertension, to lower blood pressure and reduce the risk of cardiovascular events

dosage.n: Swallow whole; do not crush or chew the extended-release tablet

dosage.d: Adjust to 2.5 to 10 mg once daily based on response, generally at intervals of not less than 2 weeks
dosage.n: Doses above 10 mg/day increase edema without much added benefit

dosage.d: Start 2.5 mg once daily; titrate cautiously

admin: Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush, chew, or divide
Take at about the same time each day, without grapefruit juice
Take consistently with respect to food (a high-fat meal can transiently increase peak levels)
Titrate at intervals of at least 2 weeks
Monitor blood pressure and look for ankle/leg swelling
moa: Felodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel antagonist. It reversibly blocks voltage-dependent L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, reducing transmembrane calcium influx. Because it is markedly more selective for vascular smooth muscle than for cardiac muscle, it produces arterial vasodilation and a fall in peripheral vascular resistance and blood pressure, with minimal negative inotropic effect at therapeutic doses. Reflex sympathetic activation may cause a mild increase in heart rate.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to felodipine or other dihydropyridines

preg: There are no adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women; animal studies showed digital/skeletal abnormalities at high doses. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the risk; other agents with more pregnancy data are often preferred.
lact: It is not known whether felodipine is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in milk, exercise caution; weigh the benefit of breastfeeding against potential risk.
renal: Pharmacokinetics are not appreciably altered by renal impairment; modification of the recommended dosage is usually not required in patients with impaired renal function.
hepatic: Patients with impaired liver function have higher felodipine plasma concentrations and reduced clearance. Start at 2.5 mg once daily and monitor closely; titrate cautiously.

major: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin) - markedly increase felodipine levels and hypotension; avoid or reduce dose
Grapefruit juice - several-fold increase in felodipine concentration; avoid
moderate: CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, rifampin) - greatly reduce felodipine effect
Tacrolimus - felodipine may increase tacrolimus levels; monitor
minor: Cimetidine - modest increase in felodipine levels
interactions.food: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice; a high-fat/high-carbohydrate meal can raise peak levels - take consistently.
interactions.alcohol: May enhance the blood-pressure-lowering effect; limit alcohol.
interactions.diagnostics: Mild reflex increase in heart rate may be seen; no characteristic lab interference.

serious: Worsening angina or myocardial infarction (rarely, on initiation/uptitration of dihydropyridines)

monitoring: Symptoms of hypotension or worsening angina
counsel: Swallow the tablet whole - do not crush or chew it
Do not drink grapefruit juice or eat grapefruit while on this medicine
Ankle/leg swelling and headache are common, especially at higher doses - report if bothersome
Stand up slowly to avoid dizziness, especially when starting
Keep taking it even when you feel well; do not stop suddenly without advice
pk: Antihypertensive effect within 2-5 hours of an oral dose
Peak plasma concentration about 2.5 to 5 hours (extended-release)
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Avoid grapefruit juice - it can raise felodipine levels several-fold via CYP3A4 inhibition
Dose-related peripheral edema is the hallmark side effect; rarely improves with dose reduction or adding an ACE inhibitor/ARB
Vascular-selective - minimal negative inotropy, so safer than some CCBs in mild LV dysfunction
Start low (2.5 mg) in elderly and hepatic impairment
Swallow whole - it is an extended-release tablet
missed: If you miss a dose, take it when you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next day's dose, skip the missed one - do not take two tablets together.
overdose: Overdose can cause marked peripheral vasodilation with pronounced hypotension and reflex tachycardia (or, with very large doses, bradycardia). Management is supportive: place the patient supine with legs elevated, give IV fluids and vasopressors as needed, monitor cardiac and renal function; intravenous calcium and atropine may help. Dialysis is not effective because of high protein binding.
